Hearing that tremendous clamour, the King of the Monkeys, 
curling and uncurling his tail, became greatly excited, whilst 
those monkeys, eager to see Rama, with Angada at their head 
and Hanuman before them, drunk with joy, alighted from the 
sky in front of their sovereign and Raghava. 
Thereafter the mighty-armed Hanuman, inclining his head 
in salutations, informed Rama of Sita's physical and spiritual 
well-being. And hearing from Hanuman the auspicious 
words sweet as Amrita : " I have seen Sita ", the joy of 
Rama and Lakshmana was extreme and Lakshmana gazed on 
Sugriva, who had placed the matter in the hands of the son of 
Pavana, with profound respect, whilst Raghava, the destroyer 
of his foes, in extreme felicity looked on Hanuman with venera-
tion.

HAVING reached the Mount Prasravana with its many woods, 
Hanuman paid obeisance to the mighty Rama and Lakshmana. 
Preceded by the heir-apparent, Angada and bowing to Sugriva 
and the monkeys, he began to recount the story of Sita and 
ber confinement in Ravma's harem, of the threats of the 
female titans, of her unflinching devotion to Rama and the 
time fixed for her execution. All this did the monkey relate 
in Rama's presence. 
And bearing of Vaidehi's well-being, Rama said:-" 0

I observed her reviled by hideous titan

lady, accustomed by thee to felicity, is now stricken with

absorbed in the thought of thee! Lying on the earth, emaciated,

brief.summary_1line: Hanuman returns to Rama, reports Sita’s captivity and steadfast devotion in Lanka, and delivers her jewel and message urging Rama to rescue her within a month.

image_candidates.scene_text: Hanuman bows before Rama and Lakshmana on Mount Prasravana, holding Sita’s radiant jewel as the gathered monkeys watch.
In the Ashoka grove, the emaciated Sita sits on the ground beneath trees, guarded by fierce demon women while she thinks only of Rama.
Sita hands her shining jewel to Hanuman as a token for Rama, her frail figure resolute despite captivity.

deep.rich_summary: After the triumphant return of the search party, the monkeys descend from the sky before Rama, their success evident in their joyful uproar. Hanuman bows and delivers the long‑awaited news: he has found Sita. Rama and Lakshmana are overwhelmed with relief and reverence for Hanuman’s achievement. At Mount Prasravana, Hanuman recounts his journey across the vast ocean to Lanka and describes Sita’s captivity in Ravana’s inner quarters, guarded by terrifying demonesses. Though emaciated with grief, she remains unwaveringly devoted to Rama and rejects Ravana’s advances. As proof of their meeting, Hanuman presents the radiant jewel she entrusted to him and relays her urgent message: she can endure only one more month in captivity. The moment confirms Sita’s fidelity and sets the stage for the coming rescue and war.

highlight_spans.why: The jubilant return of the monkeys from the sky establishes the triumphant turning point of the search for Sita.
Hanuman’s announcement that he has seen Sita—one of the most pivotal revelations in the epic—fills Rama and Lakshmana with relief.
Hanuman recounts his mythic leap across the vast ocean to Lanka and his discovery of Sita imprisoned in Ravana’s palace.
The description of Sita’s sorrowful state—emaciated, steadfast, and refusing Ravana—captures the emotional heart of the episode.
Sita’s token jewel and her urgent message to Rama serve as decisive proof of the meeting and heighten the urgency of her rescue.

top_scenes.scene_text: A host of jubilant monkeys led by Hanuman and Angada descend from the sky before Rama and Sugriva, their victory cries echoing through the forest.
Hanuman kneels before Rama and presents Sita’s radiant jewel, its light gleaming as Rama listens with intense emotion.
In the shadowed Ashoka grove of Lanka, the sorrowful Sita sits on the ground beneath trees, guarded by fearsome demonesses while clutching the jewel she will send to Rama.
